Statement from Representative Mannion on H.R. 7008 | Congressman John Mannion Skip to main content Statement from Representative Mannion on H.R. 7008 July 23, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. – Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today released the following statement:    "The American people want corruption and big money out of politics. That's why I don't trade individual stocks, I never have and I never will, as long as I am an elected official.    I believe Citizens United must be overturned, and I support real reforms like the Restore Trust in Congress Act and the Restore Trust in Government Act. Both bills would ban stock trading by the President, Vice President, Members of Congress, their spouses, and senior staff.       H.R. 7008 does the opposite, preserving opportunities for government corruption while attaching extreme voting restrictions that would make it harder for eligible Americans - including seniors, military members, women, and people with disabilities - to cast their ballots. It's clearly an attempt to sabotage our elections, sow doubt in American democracy, and make elected officials less accountable to the people they serve."   # # #    Media Press Releases Back to top button

Mannion (NY-22) Cosponsors Bipartisan Strengthening Essential Manufacturing and Industrial (SEMI) Investment Act and Semiconductor Technology Advancement and Research (STAR) Act | Congressman John Mannion Skip to main content Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) Cosponsors Bipartisan Strengthening Essential Manufacturing and Industrial (SEMI) Investment Act and Semiconductor Technology Advancement and Research (STAR) Act August 10, 2026 Press Release Extends and expands the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit to ensure continued domestic growth of semiconductor manufacturing WASHINGTON, D.C. – Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today cosponsored two bipartisan bills to extend and expand the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit (AMIC), continuing his work to make Upstate New York a national leader in semiconductor manufacturing.    The Strengthening Essential Manufacturing and Industrial (SEMI) Investment Act extends the AMIC through 2031 and expands eligibility for the CHIPS Act tax credit to include upstream materials. The Semiconductor Technology Advancement and Research (STAR) Act incentivizes research and chip design investments.    Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) said, “Semiconductor manufacturing will be the cornerstone of economic growth in Central New York and the Mohawk Valley. We need to continue making the right investments and advancing policies that support every part of the industry, from research and design to materials and manufacturing. The bipartisan SEMI Investment Act and STAR Act will help create jobs, strengthen our national security, and keep American innovation here at home.”   Strengthening Essential Manufacturing and Industrial (SEMI) Investment Act   The bipartisan SEMI Investment Act extends the AMIC through 2031, expands the CHIPS Act tax credit to include upstream materials, and requires annual materials qualification lists from Treasury and Commerce. Under current law, the term “materials” is not included in the AMIC, excluding domestic manufacturers of semiconductor materials from the tax credit. Mannion (NY-22), a member of the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), Ranking Member of the Committee, and Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01) today introduced bipartisan legislation  to protect key offices and programs at the U.S. Department of Education from being transferred through interagency agreements to other federal agencies that lack the staff, experience, and expertise needed to administer them. The legislation is the House companion to S.5046 , a bipartisan bill led by Senators Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) that advanced out of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee in July. Representative Mannion Presents Military Medals and Honors to Highly Decorated Vietnam Veteran Joe Pounder of Liverpool | Congressman John Mannion Skip to main content Representative Mannion Presents Military Medals and Honors to Highly Decorated Vietnam Veteran Joe Pounder of Liverpool August 27, 2026 Press Release SYRACUSE, NY - Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today presented military medals, unit awards, ribbons, and badges to Joe Pounder of Liverpool, a highly decorated U.S. Army veteran who served with the 5th Special Forces Group (Airborne), 1st Special Forces, during the Vietnam War. Pounder attained the rank of sergeant first class during more than a decade of service in the U.S. Army. His honors include two Bronze Star Medals, including one with a “V” device for heroism; two Purple Hearts; two Army Commendation Medals, including one with a “V” device; and the Air Medal. Representative John W. Mannion said, “Sergeant Pounder rushed into enemy fire to save four wounded members of his patrol, coordinated their evacuation, and then led his men forward against the enemy. That is extraordinary heroism, and these medals and decorations honor more than a decade of devotion to our country. It’s my privilege to help Joe receive what he earned, ensure his service will always be recognized, and give his family lasting symbols of what he did for our nation.” On October 25, 1969, Pounder was serving as a Special Forces adviser to a patrol operating from Camp Tra Bong when the unit was ambushed and four members of the patrol were wounded in the open under intense enemy fire. Pounder rushed forward and moved the wounded to cover, rallied the patrol, called for a medical evacuation, coordinated artillery and air support, and then led an assault that routed the enemy. He was awarded the Bronze Star Medal with “V” device for his heroism. Representative Mannion Calls On Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent To Place Harriet Tubman On The $20 Bill | Congressman John Mannion Skip to main content Representative Mannion Calls On Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent To Place Harriet Tubman On The $20 Bill August 17, 2026 Press Release SYRACUSE, NY — Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) sent a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calling on the Department to resume the effort to place Harriet Tubman on the $20 bill.   The bipartisan campaign to place Tubman on U.S. currency began in 2015. Last month, Secretary Bessent said that the Department was not presently planning to move forward  with the plan. Representative Mannion, joined by Congressional Black Caucus Chair Emerita Representative Joyce Beatty (OH-03), demanded an immediate resumption of the effort and a transparent timeline of the project.   The full text is below, and the formatted letter can be found here:    The Honorable Scott Bessent   Secretary of the Treasury   U.S. Department of the Treasury   1500 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW   Washington, DC 20220   Dear Secretary Bessent:  With disappointment and frustration, we write to urge the U.S. Department of the Treasury to immediately resume the now 10-year effort to place abolitionist Harriet Tubman on the twenty-dollar bill.  Harriet Tubman put her own life and freedom at risk to lead hundreds of enslaved Americans to freedom. Like the other patriots we honor on our currency, Tubman was an American hero whose extraordinary life embodied our nation’s enduring commitment to liberty and justice for all. It is long past time for our currency to recognize the historic contributions of women who helped shape the story of our nation.  This effort is especially important to New York’s 22nd Congressional District. Representative John W. Mannion Announces Federal Public Safety Funding for Utica and Oneida County | Congressman John Mannion Skip to main content Representative John W. Mannion Announces Federal Public Safety Funding for Utica and Oneida County August 13, 2026 Press Release $35,469 federal grant will support criminal investigations and alternatives to incarceration UTICA, N.Y. – Representative John W. Mannion today announced that the City of Utica and Oneida County will receive $35,469 in federal funding through the U.S. Department of Justice’s Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Program.   Representative John W. Mannion said, “Everyone deserves to live in a safe community, and this federal grant will provide local law enforcement with additional tools to fight crime and protect residents. It will support the police officers and probation professionals working every day to keep Utica and Oneida County safe.”   The Utica Police Department will use its portion of the award to increase patrols in areas experiencing high levels of violent crime and purchase equipment and software used for tactical response and criminal investigations. The Oneida County Probation Department will use the funding to strengthen supervision of individuals participating in electronic monitoring as an alternative to incarceration.   The funding was awarded by the Department of Justice’s Bureau of Justice Assistance through the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Program. The program provides federal resources to state and local governments for law enforcement, crime prevention, corrections, technology, and other public safety initiatives.       # # #   Media Press Releases Back to top button
